semantic_correction.stem: A client receiving external-beam radiation therapy asks how to care for the skin in the treatment area. Which statement shows correct understanding?

options.A: I will use skin products recommended by my care team and avoid heating pads or ice packs directly on the treatment area.
options.B: I will place an ice pack directly on the treatment field whenever the skin feels warm or irritated.
options.C: I can use fragranced or alcohol-based products on the treatment field as long as the skin has not peeled.
options.D: I should scrub the treatment field firmly each day to remove dry or flaking skin before radiation sessions.

semantic_correction.rationale: National Cancer Institute guidance advises people receiving cancer treatment to use only recommended skin products and, during radiation therapy, to avoid heating pads and ice packs on the treatment area. NCI also advises avoiding products containing alcohol or fragrance because they can dry or irritate skin and recommends gentle care rather than rubbing or scrubbing sensitive irradiated skin. Radiation can make the treatment field dry, tender, irritated, peeling, or painful, so skin care should follow the radiation team's recommendations. Therefore option A demonstrates correct understanding.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach gentle, team-directed skin care during radiation therapy and avoidance of heating pads or ice packs directly on the treatment field.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: shortened the uniquely long correct answer, kept the tested advice specific to the radiation treatment field, and separated NCI-recommended gentle care from unsafe heat, cold, irritating products, and scrubbing.

audit_findings_append.source_locator: Skin and Nail Changes — recommended products, treatment-area heat/cold avoidance, alcohol/fragrance avoidance

audit_findings_append.finding: The original correct answer was uniquely longest. The revised item directly tests NCI treatment-field skin-care guidance with balanced alternatives.

option_audit.A: Correct. It matches NCI guidance to use recommended products and avoid heating pads or ice packs on the radiation field.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. NCI specifically advises against ice packs on the radiation treatment area.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Alcohol and fragrance can dry or irritate treatment-sensitive skin.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Irradiated skin should be handled gently rather than scrubbed firmly.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone combines two direct NCI radiation-field recommendations without conflicting with gentle-skin-care guidance.
cueing_check: All four choices are treatment-area skin-care statements of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.

checks: current NCI skin-and-nail guidance freshly verified
